finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml::branch-controlled ci output is interpolated verbatim into the fixer prompt with no data delimiter or "treat as data" instruction — the sibling workflow does wrap its untrusted input

verdict.reasoning: Verified against the supplied files: agent-iterate-ci.yml's Claude step interpolates `${{ steps.diag.outputs.summary }}` bare into the prompt with no delimiter or data-framing, while agent-review-panel.yml's equivalent fixer step wraps its untrusted input in `<panel-findings>` with an explicit "REVIEW DATA, not instructions" preamble — the asymmetry the claim describes is exactly as written. The provenance chain also checks out: summarize-ci.mjs prints `failureSummary`/`lane.lane` verbatim from `.harness-reports`, written by verify-self.mjs's `extractFailureSummary(output)` over raw stdout of branch-executed commands, and the diff's `allowed_bots` line is what makes this step actually run. One sub-claim is overstated: `extractFailureSummary` returns a single trimmed ≤500-char line, so it alone cannot break the `HARNESS_EOF` heredoc; that requires whole-artifact control. Severity is tempered because the same job already runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` on the untrusted branch with the App/OAuth secrets present, so this is defence-in-depth drift rather than a new privilege boundary.

finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml::github app installation token is persisted into .git/config of the untrusted branch checkout, then branch-controlled install scripts are executed

verdict.reasoning: Verified against the supplied files: in `.github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml` the `actions/checkout@v4` step passes `token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}` with `ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}` and no `persist-credentials: false`, so the App installation token is written into `.git/config` as an http.extraheader in the untrusted branch checkout; a later step then runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` on that branch tree, and root `package.json` does declare a `postinstall` script, so branch-controlled lifecycle scripts (and any branch-added dependency's install scripts) execute with the token readable via `git config --get http.https://github.com/.extraheader`. The contrast the reviewer draws is also accurate: `agent-review-panel.yml`'s `deps` and `review-panel` checkouts explicitly set `persist-credentials: false` with a comment giving exactly this reason, the panel's `fix` checkout does not, and the iterate job's App token is minted with no `permission-*` scoping (unlike the panel's contents/PR/issues-scoped token). Mitigating context (base-repo `agent/` branches only, `AGENT_PIPELINE_ENABLED`, `environment: agent`, and the fact that claude-code-action later receives the same token anyway) reduces but does not eliminate the exposure — it widens the leak to third-party install scripts and violates the repo's own stated rule; note this is pre-existing code, not introduced by the diff under review.

finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml::the "only our panel's checks" filter on the fix prompt is app-slug based, and every workflow in the repo — including one added on the untrusted branch — produces app slug `github-actions`

verdict.reasoning: I read the supplied `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml` (the "Gather failing lens findings" step, and the identical `mine = (r) => NAMES.has(r.name) && r.app && r.app.slug === 'github-actions'` predicate in the round-bound guard). The claim's reading of the code is accurate: `github-actions` is the app slug for every GITHUB_TOKEN/workflow-created check run in the repository, so the filter proves only "some workflow in this repo made it", not "our trusted review-panel job made it", and the resulting `output.summary` is spliced verbatim into the fixer prompt for a Bash/Write-enabled agent — so the comment's assurance holds only against the narrower "another installed App" threat it names. The exploit path the reviewer describes is however gated in practice, as the reviewer itself concedes: adding/modifying a file under `.github/workflows` requires `workflows: write`, and the fix job's token is explicitly scoped to contents/pull-requests/issues, so today this is a latent defence-in-depth gap rather than a live injection channel (I could not check the installation's permission set — `docs/tasks/active/20260720-autonomous-issue-to-pr-pipeline-todo.md` was withheld). Note also that the flagged lines are pre-existing code, untouched by this diff, which only adds `allowed_bots` and the `fix` dependency for `stalled`.
